claims.text: Effect, PR: mildly prolonged, up to 240 ms (↑vagal tone)
claims.quote: Mild PR interval prolongation, up to 240 ms (due to increased vagal tone)

claims.text: Effect = ⍉toxicity: digoxin effect only shows that the pt = taking digoxin
claims.quote: Note: The presence of digoxin effect on the ECG is not a marker of digoxin toxicity. It merely indicates that the patient is taking digoxin.

claims.text: Toxicity, rhythm: virtually any arrhythmia; classic: atrial tachy w block, ↔ VT, freq PVCs
claims.quote: Toxicity: Virtually any arrhythmia, but classic findings include atrial tachycardia with block, bidirectional VT, frequent PVCs
claims.locator: 12. Important "Can't-Miss" Patterns, Digoxin Effect vs. Toxicity

claims.text: Classic toxic rhythm: SVT (↑automaticity) w a slow ventricular response (↓AV conduction)
claims.quote: The classic digoxin toxic dysrhythmia combines: Supraventricular tachycardia (due to increased automaticity) Slow ventricular response (due to decreased AV conduction)

claims.text: MC abnormality: freq PVCs, incl ventricular bigeminy and trigeminy
claims.quote: Frequent PVCs (the most common abnormality), including ventricular bigeminy and trigeminy

claims.text: Also: sinus brady, slow AF, any AV block (1st, 2nd or 3rd degree), “regularized” AF (AF w complete ♡ block and a junctional or ventricular escape), VT incl polymorphic and ↔
claims.quote: Sinus bradycardia Slow Atrial Fibrillation Any type of AV block (1st degree, 2nd degree & 3rd degree) Regularised AF = AF with complete heart block and a junctional or ventricular escape rhythm Ventricular tachycardia, including polymorphic and bidirectional VT

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Effect: seen @ therapeutic doses
claims.quote: The ECG features of digoxin effect are seen with therapeutic doses of digoxin

claims.text: Effect mech: shorter atrial and ventricular refractory periods → short QT w 2/2 ST, T and U wave chgs; ↑vagal effect @ the AV node → longer PR
claims.quote: Shortening of the atrial and ventricular refractory periods — producing a short QT interval with secondary repolarisation abnormalities affecting the ST segments, T waves and U waves Increased vagal effects at the AV node — causing a prolonged PR interval

claims.text: Toxicity mech: ↑automaticity (more intracell calcium) and ↓AV conduction (↑vagal effect @ the AV node)
claims.quote: Digoxin can cause a multitude of dysrhythmias due to: Increased automaticity (increased intracellular calcium) Decreased AV conduction (increased vagal effects at the AV node)

claims.text: Visual: blurred vision, yellow/green discoloration, haloes
claims.quote: Visual: Blurred vision, yellow/green discolouration, haloes

claims.text: Tx (toxicity) Antidote: digoxin-specific Fab fragments (for digitalis glycosides: digoxin, digitoxin, oleander, foxglove)
claims.quote: Digitalis glycosides (eg, digoxin, digitoxin, oleander, foxglove) | Digoxin-specific Fab fragments

claims.quote: Calcium antagonizes the effect of hyperkalemia on cardiac muscle. Calcium should be given with caution to patients taking digoxin because of the risk of precipitating hypokalemia-related arrhythmias.
